blocks.x: Products enforce; architecture decides where trust dies.

Zero-trust is an architecture, not a purchase rests on one claim: enterprises that industrialize measurement ship faster and defend it in audit. The pages that follow show the mechanics, not just the claim.

items: Trust-tier migration sequences the estate so value lands in months, not years.
Workload identity (SPIFFE-class) closes the service-to-service trust gap humans ignore.
Evidence packs mapped to ISO 27001/SOC 2 turn certification into collection.

blocks.x: Three questions to ask your current vendors

items: Ask for the baseline: how was the starting position measured, and who signed it?
Ask for the trail: can your auditors replay any decision the system made last week, end to end?
Ask for the unit cost: what does one decision cost to run, and who owns keeping it down?

blocks.x: Programs like Zero-trust is an architecture, not a purchase rarely fail on the technology. They fail on unnamed ownership, unmeasured baselines and ungated scope — the three failure modes the guards on this page are built for.

items: Every stage has a gate with real stop authority — scope expands on measured deltas, not on momentum.
The operating model is designed first — who decides what, at which gate, holding which evidence.
Evidence is generated while the work happens, so the audit is a walkthrough, not an archaeology project.

blocks.x: Mature programs measure residual implicit trust — and drive it to near zero.
